pr.title: tcp: preserve the receive window advertised to the peer
pr.head: 97aa81bc43f6d417a8a082c48f98adb87bb203ef

items.body:
LGTM. This is a small fix that keeps `rcvWnd` consistent with what goes on the wire, and it matches Linux's `tcp_select_window()`, which stores the scale-aligned `new_win` in `tp->rcv_wnd`. The test extension reproduces the premature reopen after a scaled-zero advertisement. The PR rebases cleanly on current master. Optional nits:

1. `receiver.acceptable()` is now partly redundant. Its comment ("r.rcvWnd could be much larger than the window size we advertised") is no longer true, and its clamp/round-down is a no-op. Consider simplifying it to `RcvNxt.Add(r.rcvWnd)`, here or in a follow-up.
2. Consider pointing the new `rcv.go` comment at the Linux equivalent (`tcp_select_window()`) rather than listing the consumers.
3. FYI: Linux rounds the retained window up (`ALIGN(cur_win, 1 << rcv_wscale)`) so it never shrinks. gVisor rounds down. Now that the rounded value is stored, the keep-current-window branch can move the right edge left by up to `2^wscale−1` per ACK when `toGrow` is false. The grow branch corrects it for MSS-sized traffic, so I don't think it needs changing, but a sentence in the commit message would help future readers.

**Security:** No security impact. The change only makes `r.rcvWnd` match the scale-aligned window that is actually advertised, which can only make it smaller. It adds no host interactions, allocations, locks, or panics, and the shift cannot overflow because `scaledWnd ≤ 0xFFFF` and the locally chosen scale is at most 14. Peer- and app-driven inputs reach the same bounded window and buffer logic as before.

---

Lucas found that rounding could withdraw space already advertised. The receiver now preserves those bytes, and the wire test checks the right edge as well as the zero-window probe you reviewed.

Posted by Codex on behalf of @tamird.

Thanks, this addresses everything. acceptable() now uses the stored window, and the retained window rounds up like Linux's ALIGN(cur_win, 1 << rcv_wscale) in tcp_select_window(), so already-advertised space is never retracted. The extended test covers both the right edge and the scaled-zero probe. LGTM.

---
[🤖] This review is part of an experimental auto-review process to help speed up gVisor review velocity. It is a work in progress. Assisted-by: Claude

Nit: suggest `// Like Linux's tcp_select_window(), remember the window as the peer decodes it.` instead of listing consumers.

Follow-up: with `r.rcvWnd` now always `<= MaxUint16 << RcvWndScale` and scale-aligned, the clamp/round-down in `acceptable()` is a no-op. Its comment ("r.rcvWnd could be much larger than the window size we advertised") is also stale. Consider simplifying it to `header.Acceptable(segSeq, segLen, r.RcvNxt, r.RcvNxt.Add(r.rcvWnd))`.

FYI: Linux rounds the retained window up in the no-shrink path (`ALIGN(cur_win, 1 << rcv_wscale)` in `tcp_select_window()`), but this rounds down. Now that the rounded value is stored, the `else { newWnd = curWnd }` branch can move the right edge left by up to `2^wscale-1` per ACK when `toGrow` is false (MSS-sized traffic gets corrected by the grow branch). Fine by me given this test's scaled-zero premise; maybe mention it in the commit message.

[The wire test](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/d6e64bdd-82d4-483a-8c68-ee426eaacdd4) now checks that every ACK covers the unconsumed bytes. [The amended receiver](https://github.com/tamird/gvisor/commit/f5e35772f5ff7143e634613dc55a0e2356556cec) rounds up when rounding down would retract that space. source.title: tcp: remember the advertised receive window
source.body:
tcp: remember the advertised receive window

After advertising a zero window, a probe following a partial application
read received a 50,016-byte window even though the available space
remained below the reopening threshold. Window scaling had discarded low
bits from the packet header but left them in rcvWnd, so the probe
skipped zero-window reopening checks.

Store the decoded advertised window after scaling and capping it. Extend
the existing scaled-window test with a partial read and a probe that
must still receive a zero-window ACK, before the remaining read reopens
it.

FUTURE_COPYBARA_INTEGRATE_REVIEW=https://github.com/google/gvisor/pull/16382 from tamird:fix/tcp-advertised-window-state f5e35772f5ff7143e634613dc55a0e2356556cec

source.title: tcp: preserve the receive window advertised to the peer
source.body:
tcp: preserve the receive window advertised to the peer

Window scaling discards low bits from the receive window. Remembering
the larger, unscaled value can make a zero-window probe reopen the
window before the application has drained enough data. Conversely,
rounding down the remaining window after a partial segment can
withdraw space already offered to data in flight.

Store the window as the peer decodes it. When rounding down would move
the right edge left, round up one window unit, as Linux does in
tcp_select_window() [1]. Use that same window when deciding whether
to accept an incoming segment.

Exercise both edges on the wire: ACK a byte inside the last window
unit without retracting the rest, then exhaust the window and check
that a partial read does not reopen it.

[1]: https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/fe584bc4c81b02bab4766513d57a33f5f4af02b3/net/ipv4/tcp_output.c#L295-L309
